outcomes.text: kutambua nafasi ya pambizo na nafasi ya kuzingatia anapoandika aya
kuandika kifungu cha maneno yasiyozidi 60 akizingatia pambizo na aya
kufurahia kuandika kifungu akizingatia pambizo na aya

skills.name: Andika kifungu ukizingatia pambizo, aya na nafasi kati ya maneno
skills.mastery: Writes a passage of up to 60 words that keeps out of the margin, leaves space between words, starts a new aya for a new idea and breaks a long word at the end of a line only between syllables, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: A neat passage comes before laying it out with margins and aya.
Space between words (Grade 2) is the first rule of layout.

misconceptions.error: Writes into the margin, from the edge of the page.

example.question: Pambizo ni nini?
example.correct_answer: nafasi iliyoachwa ukingoni mwa ukurasa bila maandishi

misconceptions.cause: The child wants to fit more on the page and does not see the margin line as a rule.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Pambizo ni nini?" with "sehemu ya kuandikia kwanza" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Colour the margin; nothing may enter the coloured strip.
misconceptions.feedback: Usiandike ndani ya pambizo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes everything in one block with no new aya.
misconceptions.cause: The child has not been shown that a new idea gets a new aya.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaanza aya mpya lini?" with "sianzi; ninaandika kila kitu pamoja" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a passage with two ideas; the child marks where the second starts.
misconceptions.feedback: Wazo jipya, aya mpya.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Starts every sentence on a new line, as if each were an aya.

example.question: Kila sentensi ianze mstari mpya?
example.correct_answer: hapana; sentensi za wazo moja hufuatana katika aya moja

misconceptions.cause: Early copying from the board was one sentence a line.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kila sentensi ianze mstari mpya?" with "ndiyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Rewrite three sentences about one idea as one aya.
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi za wazo moja hukaa pamoja katika aya moja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Breaks a word at the end of a line in the middle of a syllable (mkul-ima).

example.question: Neno ni refu na mstari umeisha. Ni mgawanyo upi sahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The child cuts where the space ends, not at a syllable.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno ni refu na mstari umeisha. Ni mgawanyo upi sahihi?" with "mkul-ima" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the syllables first; break only between two claps, with a dash.
misconceptions.feedback: Gawa neno kati ya silabi na uweke kistari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

kujaza nafasi kwa kukamilisha sentensi katika umoja na wingi akiwa na mwenzake,

kuandika sentensi katika umoja na wingi
kuchangamkia kutumia umoja na wingi katika sentensi

skills.name: Andika sentensi za kazi mbalimbali katika umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Writes sentences about workers in singular and plural: people nouns take wa- (mwalimu - walimu, mpishi - wapishi), li-ma nouns take ma- or change (daktari - madaktari, jino - meno), and the verb agrees, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Changing a sentence to the plural (Theme 2) comes first.
Writing singular and plural word groups (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "Mwalimu anafundisha" ni?" with "Mialimu inafundisha." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (Walimu wanafundisha.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Changes the noun but not the verb or the word that agrees with it (Vitabu kimeanguka).

example.question: Andika kwa wingi: Daktari anatibu wagonjwa.

misconceptions.cause: The child changes the word he was asked to change and stops there.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika kwa wingi: Daktari anatibu wagonjwa." with "Madaktari anatibu wagonjwa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Colour the noun prefix and the verb prefix the same; read the sentence and check every coloured part.
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi nzima hubadilika: Vitabu vimeanguka. (Madaktari wanatibu wagonjwa.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
misconceptions.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika kwa wingi: Jino linauma." with "Majino yanauma." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
misconceptions.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (Meno yanauma.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
misconceptions.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mpishi mmoja" ni?" with "mpishi wawili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (wapishi wawili)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusikiliza kifungu cha maneno 60-65 kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali ili kutambua ujumbe unaowasilishwa,
kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia msamiati aliousikiliza kwenye kifungu,
kujibu maswali yanayohusiana na kifungu alichosikiliza,
kujadili mambo muhimu katika kifungu alichokisikiliza akiwa na wenzake,
kusimulia wenzake upya kifungu alichokisikiliza.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia mambo gani ili kuelewa mambo unayoelezewa?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na kuwasiliana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali katika ujifunzaji.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli za huduma kwa jamii kwa kusimulia visa vyepesi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anaposimulia upya kifungu alichokisikiliza.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu maoni ya wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anapowashirikisha wengine katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali darasani.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anaposimulia wenzake upya kifungu alichokisoma.
sub_strands.pcis: Masuala ya usalama: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza na kuzungumzia masuala ya usalama.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kusikiliza na kuzungumza anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa stadi hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua ujumbe unaowasilishwa katika kifungu
kutambua msamiati uliotumiwa katika kifungu alichosikiliza
kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia msamiati uliotumika kwenye kifungu alichosikiliza
kusimulia upya kifungu cha hadithi winalichokisikiliza
kuchangamkia kusikiliza kifungu

skills.name: Sikiliza kifungu, eleza ujumbe na msamiati wake, na usimulie upya
skills.mastery: After hearing a short passage (Wanjiru alivuka barabara bila kuangalia na nusura agongwe na gari), says its message, gives the meaning of a new word from it, uses the word in a sentence of his own and retells the events in order, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying the message of a heard story in Grade 2 comes first.
Finding the message and new words of a read passage is the same work as for a heard one.

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tuangalie kulia na kushoto na kuvuka kwenye kivuko ili tuwe salama.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is the clearest thing the child remembers; he has not been asked what the passage teaches.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?" with "Wanjiru alienda dukani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: After listening, ask "Kifungu kinatufundisha nini?" and compare it with "Nini kilitokea?".
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tuangalie kulia na kushoto na kuvuka kwenye kivuko ili tuwe salama.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives "kivuko" the meaning of a word that sounds like it.

example.question: Neno "kivuko" katika kifungu lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the sound of the word to one he knows instead of listening to the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "kivuko" katika kifungu lina maana gani?" with "kivuli" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Replay the sentence; the child tries each meaning in it and keeps the one that makes sense.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "kivuko" ni mahali palipotengwa pa kuvuka barabara.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes a "sentence" that only repeats the word and shows no meaning (kivuko ni kivuko).

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kivuko"?
example.correct_answer: Tulivuka barabara kwenye kivuko cha watembea kwa miguu.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks any sentence with the word in it is enough.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kivuko"?" with "Kivuko ni kivuko." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: if your friend did not know the word, would your sentence tell him what it means?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi nzuri inaonyesha maana ya neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells the events out of order.

example.question: Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea.
example.wrong_answer: Gari lilisimama ghafla, Wanjiru alienda dukani, alivuka barabara bila kuangalia
example.correct_answer: Wanjiru alienda dukani, alivuka barabara bila kuangalia, gari likasimama ghafla

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers the most exciting event and tells it first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea." with "Gari lilisimama ghafla, Wanjiru alienda dukani, alivuka barabara bila kuangalia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Three picture cards of the events; the child lays them left to right and retells with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Matukio yalifuatana hivi: Wanjiru alienda dukani, alivuka barabara bila kuangalia, gari likasimama ghafla.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Adds events that were not in the passage when retelling.

example.question: Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?

misconceptions.cause: Retelling is taken as storytelling: the child invents to make it longer.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?" with "ndiyo, ili hadithi iwe tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: After the retelling, the class checks each event: was it in the passage? Thumbs up or down.
misconceptions.feedback: Kusimulia upya ni kusema yaliyokuwa kwenye kifungu tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 60 - 65 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutabiri kitakachotokea katika hadithi akizingatia picha kwenye kifungu,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutabiri ujumbe wa kifungu kwa kutazama picha kwenye kitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali au chati akiwa na wenzake,
kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu hadithi baada ya kuisoma,
kufafanua mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu kuhusu usalama wake shuleni.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo gani unapaswa kuzingatia ili kufanikisha usomaji bora?

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on usalama, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The comprehension questions of Theme 3 come first.
Predicting from a short passage in Grade 2.

misconceptions.error: Gives "waya" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Hawa aliona waya wa umeme umeanguka karibu na njia. Alikumbuka maneno ya mwalimu: usiguse waya wa umeme. Alimwita baba mara moja." Neno "waya" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Hawa aliona waya wa umeme umeanguka karibu na njia. Alikumbuka maneno ya mwalimu: usiguse waya wa umeme. Alimwita baba mara moja." Neno "waya" lina maana gani?" with "mayai" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "waya" ni uzi wa chuma unaopitisha umeme.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tusiguse waya wa umeme; tuwaite watu wazima.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Hawa alikuwa njiani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tusiguse waya wa umeme; tuwaite watu wazima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha baba akipiga simu. Baba atafanya nini?
example.correct_answer: Atawapigia wataalamu wa umeme waje kuurekebisha.

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha baba akipiga simu. Baba atafanya nini?" with "Atashika waya kwa mkono." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Atawapigia wataalamu wa umeme waje kuurekebisha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.

example.question: Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?
example.correct_answer: Tunapaswa kuepuka hatari na kuwaeleza watu wazima.

misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Hawa aliona waya njiani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kuepuka hatari na kuwaeleza watu wazima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Hawa alimwita nani?" with "Mimi ningempigia mama simu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: Baba
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua alama ya kiulizi kutoka kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kujadili na wenzake matumizi ya alama ya kiulizi ili kukuza uwezo wa kuitumia ipasavyo,
kunakili ipasavyo kifungu kilichotumia alama ya kiulizi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuandika kifungu cha maneno kati ya 55-60 akizingatia matumizi ya alama ya kiulizi kuhusu suala lengwa, na jinsi ya kuzingatia alama za usalama barabarani kisha kuwasomea wenzake ili waitolee maoni.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, alama ya kiulizi inatumika vipi katika uandishi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapowasomea kifungu alichoandika kwa kutumia alama kiulizi.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika kifungu kwa kutumia alama ya kiulizi ipasavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika ujifunzaji na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowatambua na kuwathamini wenzake wakati wa kushiriki katika shughuli za kuandika.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia alama ya kiulizi katika maandishi na pia anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali.
sub_strands.pcis:
Usalama mtandaoni: mwanafunzi anapoelekezwa kutangamana na mitandao ya kijamii kwa njia salama.
Masuala ya usalama: mwanafunzi anapoandika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala la usalama.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya matumizi ya kiulizi anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua alama ya kiulizi katika maandishi
kueleza matumizi ya alama ya kiulizi katika maandishi
kuandika kifungu cha maneno kati ya 55-60 akitumia alama ya kiulizi ipasavyo
kufurahia kutumia kiulizi katika maandishi ili kufanikisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Tumia alama ya kiulizi ipasavyo katika maandishi
skills.mastery: Tells a question from a statement, ends each with its mark (? or .), starts the next sentence with a capital, and writes a passage of about 55-60 words with the marks in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Using the kiulizi in a sentence (Grade 2) comes first.
A capital letter follows the kiulizi.

misconceptions.error: Ends a question with a kikomo.
misconceptions.cause: The child ends every sentence the same way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Unaenda wapi" with "Unaenda wapi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the sentence aloud: if the voice rises and asks, it takes a kiulizi.
misconceptions.feedback: Swali huishia kwa kiulizi (?).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a kiulizi after a statement.

example.question: Weka alama sahihi: Mimi ninaenda sokoni

misconceptions.cause: The child uses ? as a decoration or thinks any sentence about himself is a question.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Mimi ninaenda sokoni" with "Mimi ninaenda sokoni?" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: does the sentence want an answer? If not, kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi ya kueleza huishia kwa kikomo (.).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a kiulizi after a reported question (Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi?).

example.question: Weka alama sahihi: Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi

misconceptions.cause: The question word wapi makes the child think the sentence is a question; it only tells that one was asked.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi" with "Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi?" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Compare "Unaenda wapi?" (asked now) with "Aliniuliza ninaenda wapi." (told).
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi hii inaeleza kwamba swali liliulizwa; huishia kwa kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts several kiulizi (???) for a strong question.
misconceptions.cause: Text messages and cartoons use many marks; the child copies them.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Je, tunavuka barabara wapi???" among the options.
misconceptions.help: One question, one kiulizi; show a page from the class reader.
misconceptions.feedback: Swali moja, kiulizi kimoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a small letter after a kikomo or kiulizi.

example.question: Ni lipi sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Tunavuka barabara kwenye kivuko. mama alifurahi.
example.correct_answer: Tunavuka barabara kwenye kivuko. Mama alifurahi.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not link the mark to the capital that follows it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Tunavuka barabara kwenye kivuko. mama alifurahi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Every kikomo is a gate: the next word starts big.
misconceptions.feedback: Baada ya kikomo, herufi kubwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya -ake na –ao kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, mti maneno, kapu maneno au chati akiwa na wenzake,
kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo unaotumia –ake na –ao kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa, au vifaa vya kidijitali,
kusoma kifungu kilichotumia -ake na -ao akiwa na wenzake,
kuigiza matumizi ya -ake na -ao akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi kwa kutumia vitu anavyomiliki (k.v kiti chake – viti vyao),
kutunga sentensi akitumia -ake na -ao na kuzijadili na mwenzake ili kuzitolea maoni,
kujaza nafasi ili kukamilisha sentensi zilizotumia -ake na-ao,
kumtungia mzazi au mlezi sentensi zilizo na -ake na -ao kwa kurejelea vitu mbalimbali nyumbani.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, -ake na -ao hutumiwa vipi katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anapomtungia mwenzake sentensi akitumia -ake na -ao.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na mzazi au mlezi wake kutumia -ake na –ao kwa kurejelea vitu mbalimbali nyumbani.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo kuhusu matumizi ya-ake na - ao.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapomtungia mwenzake sentensi kwa kutumia -ake na -ao.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu michango ya wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapochukua nafasi mbalimbali katika shughuli za kikundi na anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali anavyotumia.
sub_strands.pcis: Masuala ya usalama: mwanafunzi anapotangamana na wenzake katika kikundi kutunga sentensi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kutumia -ake na -ao.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya sarufi anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: no lessons figure.

outcomes.text: kutambua matumizi ya -ake na -ao katika mawasiliano
kutumia -ake na -ao katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano
kufurahia kutumia - ake na -ao ili kufanikisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Tumia -ake na -ao ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses -ake for one owner and -ao for many owners, with the noun-class prefix of the thing owned (kiti chake, viti vyao, kofia yake), placed after the noun, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: -ako and -enu (Grade 2) show the owner pattern first.
The ngeli of the thing owned sets the prefix of the possessive.

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong noun-class form of the possessive (kitabu yangu for kitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: Town Kiswahili uses yangu, yako, yake for every noun; the child has not seen the ngeli agreement.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kiti ___ (cha Juma) kimevunjika." with "yake" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair nouns and possessives by colour: kitabu changu, kiti chake, mtoto wangu.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu changu; kiti chake: kimilikishi hufuata ngeli. (chake)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the possessive singular with a plural noun (vitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun and forgets the possessive.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Viatu ___ (vya Juma) ni vipya." with "chake" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change one object to many in front of the child; both words change.
misconceptions.feedback: Vitabu vyangu: vyote viwili hubadilika. (vyake)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the possessive of the wrong owner (-ake for something that is his own, -ake for many owners).
misconceptions.cause: The child has not linked -angu, -ako, -ake, -etu, -enu, -ao to who owns the thing.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Watoto wana mpira. Ni mpira ___." with "wake" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up an object: Ni cha nani? Answer with the owner first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Mwenye kitu ni nani? Mimi: changu; yeye: chake; wao: chao. (wao)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the possessive before the noun (yangu kalamu), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts "my" before the noun; Kiswahili puts it after.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "yake kofia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build the phrase with cards: the noun first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza, kimilikishi baadaye: kalamu yangu. (kofia yake)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /dh/, /th/, /ch/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /dh/, /th/, /ch/ in syllables and words (dhahabu, thelathini, chupa), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Knowing that dh, th and ch are each one consonant comes from the vowels and consonants sub-strand.
Hearing the syllables of target sounds in words and sentences (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Says /z/ for /dh/, so "dhahabu" becomes "zahabu".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "dhahabu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /dh/, or do not separate it from /z/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "dhahabu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "zahabu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "dhahabu" ina sauti /dh/, si /z/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /sh/ for /ch/, so "chai" becomes "shai".
misconceptions.cause: /ch/ and /sh/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "shai" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "chai" ina sauti /ch/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops part of the target sound, so "thelathini" becomes "telatini".

example.question: Neno "thelathini" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The second part of the sound (the w or y glide, or the soft nasal) is quick and quiet; the child does not hear it and leaves it out.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "thelathini" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?" with "telatini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stretch the syllable slowly (p-y-a), then say it fast; the child copies.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "thelathini". Usiache sehemu ya sauti.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "dhahabu" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "dhahabu" lina silabi zipi?" with "d-h-a-h-a-b-u" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: dha-ha-bu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /dh/, /th/, /ch/?" with "mama" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "thelathini" ina sauti lengwa; "mama" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa sauti inayosikika akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 51 kwa dakika na kwa kuzingatia viakifishi),
kusoma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo akishirikiana na wenzake,

sub_strands.values:

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /dh/, /th/, /ch/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /dh/, /th/, /ch/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 51 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying dh, th and ch comes before reading them aloud.
Reading a short story at a fitting pace (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "thamani" as "samani".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "thamani" linasomwa vipi?" with "samani" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "thamani" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunatupa taka katika pipa la taka."?
example.wrong_answer: Tunatupa ... taka ... katika ... pipa ... la ... taka.
example.correct_answer: Tunatupa taka katika pipa la taka.

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunatupa taka katika pipa la taka."?" with "Tunatupa ... taka ... katika ... pipa ... la ... taka." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 51 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umeokota chupa thelathini?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umeokota chupa thelathini?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika maneno yanayotamkwa kwenye imla kwa tahajia sahihi
skills.mastery: Writes the words the teacher reads (about 55-60 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Hearing dh, th and ch clearly comes before writing them from dictation.
Writing three-syllable words from dictation (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "thelathini" written "selasini".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "selasini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "thelathini" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "ndoo" written "doo".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "doo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "ndoo" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "saa" written "sa".

example.question: Andika neno lenye maana ya "kifaa cha kuonyesha wakati".

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "kifaa cha kuonyesha wakati"." with "sa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "saa" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia -eupe, -eusi na -ekundu ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses the colour stems -eupe, -eusi and -ekundu after the noun with the right noun-class prefix and its sound change (kiti cheupe, nguo nyeupe, mfuko mweusi, mifuko myeusi), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Knowing the ngeli and its plural comes before the agreement of an adjective.
-refu, -kubwa and -tamu (Grade 2) are the first adjectives that agree.

misconceptions.error: Writes the colour word without the sound change (kiti kieupe for kiti cheupe; nguo eupe for nguo nyeupe).
misconceptions.cause: The child sticks the prefix on the stem; the sound change when ki- or n- meets the vowel (ki + eupe = cheupe) is new.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kiti ___ (-eupe)." with "kieupe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the joined forms slowly: ki-eupe becomes cheupe; n-eupe becomes nyeupe.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiti cheupe; nguo nyeupe; mtoto mweusi. (cheupe)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an n-n noun the m- form of the adjective (nyumba mzuri for nyumba nzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The n- prefix and its sound changes (nzuri, ndefu, nyeupe) are new to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Nguo ___ (-eusi)." with "mweusi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: nyumba nzuri, kalamu ndefu, nguo nyeupe.
misconceptions.feedback: Nyumba nzuri; nguo nyeupe. (nyeusi)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the adjective the people prefix whatever the noun (kiti mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: Mzuri is the form the child hears most (mtoto mzuri) and is used everywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kikombe ___ (-ekundu)." with "mwekundu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Match noun and adjective by colour: kiti kizuri, mtoto mzuri, vitu vizuri.
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi hufuata ngeli: kiti kizuri. (chekundu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the adjective before the noun (mzuri mtoto), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts the describing word first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "nyeupe karatasi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build with cards: noun first, then the adjective.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza: mtoto mzuri. (karatasi nyeupe)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the adjective singular with a plural noun (watoto mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun only.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Mifuko ___ (-eusi)." with "mweusi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change the noun to many and ask the child to change every word that goes with it.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto wazuri: vyote hubadilika. (myeusi)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua aina mbalimbali za maagizo kwenye kitabu, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kushirikiana na wenzake katika kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi kama vile (k.v. simama uende uufungue mlango),
kutazama video ya jinsi ya kutoa na kufuata maagizo kutoka kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua aina mbalimbali za maagizo akiwa na wenzake,
kuimba nyimbo na kukariri mashairi mepesi yanayohusu maagizo akiwa na wenzake,
kumwimbia mzazi au mlezi wake wimbo unaoashiria maagizo ili atoe maoni yake.
key_inquiry_questions: Je,ni kwa nini mtu hufuata yale anayoambiwa?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika masimulizi na wenzake ya kufuata na kutofuata maagizo.
Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotoa maoni katika majadiliano kuhusu jinsi ya kufuata maagizo.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoigiza maagizo mepesi akishirikiana na wenzake.
sub_strands.values:
Amani: mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi katika kikundi na wenzake kwa utulivu.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia na kutunza vifaa vya kidijitali.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotazama video ya jinsi ya kutoa na kufuata maagizo kutoka kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali bila usimamizi.
sub_strands.pcis: Elimu ya kifedha: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mazungumzo kuhusu matumizi ya pesa dukani.
sub_strands.links:

Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha suala la dukani na yanayofundishwa katika somo la Mathematics Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua maagizo mepesi yanapotolewa darasani
kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi yanayotumiwa darasani
kufurahia kuzingatia maagizo katika maisha ya kila siku

skills.name: Fuata na utoe maagizo mepesi kwa usahihi
skills.mastery: Follows a one- or two-step instruction in the right order, reads the direction and action words in it (simama, keti, kulia, kushoto, juu, chini), and gives a clear, polite instruction that names what to do and to what, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Giving and following two-step instructions in Grade 2 comes first.
A polite instruction uses tafadhali.

misconceptions.error: Carries out only the first part of a two-step instruction.

example.question: Agizo: "Chukua kikapu, kisha uende dukani." Umefanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child starts acting as soon as he hears the first verb and stops listening.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Chukua kikapu, kisha uende dukani." Umefanya nini?" with "anachukua kikapu tu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up one finger for each step while giving the instruction; the child repeats the steps before moving.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza agizo lote kwanza, kisha fanya hatua zote.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does the steps in the wrong order.

example.question: Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?

misconceptions.cause: The child does the step he wants most first; the order words kwanza and kisha are not yet noticed.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?" with "kula chakula" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Number the steps on the board with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno "kisha" linaonyesha hatua inayofuata.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes a direction or action word.

example.question: Agizo: "Weka sukari upande wa kulia wa meza." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?

misconceptions.cause: Pairs such as kulia/kushoto and juu/chini are learnt together and swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Weka sukari upande wa kulia wa meza." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?" with "anaiweka upande wa kushoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Play "Mwalimu anasema": the teacher calls the word, the child acts it; mark the right hand with a band.
misconceptions.feedback: Weka sukari upande wa kulia wa meza. maana yake ni anaiweka upande wa kulia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an instruction that leaves out what to act on, or with no polite word (Lete!).

example.question: Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what he means and does not see that the listener cannot.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?" with "Lete!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: The child gives the instruction to a partner, who does exactly what was said and no more.
misconceptions.feedback: Agizo zuri linasema nini kifanyike, kwa kitu gani, na kwa adabu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 65 - 70 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v duka, bidhaa, pesa, uza, nunua, chenji, mteja, muuzaji) akiwa na wenzake,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akiwa na wenzake,
kutabiri ujumbe wa kifungu kwa kutazama picha kwenye kitabu akiwa na wenzake,
kutabiri kitakachotokea katika kifungu chepesi akizingatia picha akiwa na wenzake,
kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu kifungu baada ya kukisoma,
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,
kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akiwa na wenzake.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia mambo gani unaposoma kifungu cha hadithi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kazi ya kikundi na kushiriki kikamilifu wanapotabiri na kujadili ujumbe katika kifungu.
Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotoa na kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu kitakachotokea katika hadithi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposoma majarida na magazeti kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kujadili picha na kutabiri kitakachotokea katika hadithi.
Haki za kijamii: mwanafunzi anapowapa wenzake fursa ya kujieleza katika shughuli za kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotabiri kilichotokea katika kifungu alichokisoma.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on dukani, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The comprehension questions of Theme 5 come first.
Saying the message of a short passage (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Gives "chenji" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Mama alimpa Otieno shilingi mia moja. Otieno alinunua mkate wa shilingi sitini na maziwa ya shilingi thelathini. Muuzaji alimrudishia chenji." Neno "chenji" lina maana gani?
example.correct_answer: pesa zinazorudishwa baada ya kulipa zaidi

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Mama alimpa Otieno shilingi mia moja. Otieno alinunua mkate wa shilingi sitini na maziwa ya shilingi thelathini. Muuzaji alimrudishia chenji." Neno "chenji" lina maana gani?" with "chupa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "chenji" ni pesa zinazorudishwa baada ya kulipa zaidi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tunapaswa kuhesabu pesa vizuri tunaponunua bidhaa.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Otieno alinunua mkate." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tunapaswa kuhesabu pesa vizuri tunaponunua bidhaa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for.

example.question: Otieno atampa mama nini akirudi nyumbani?
example.correct_answer: mkate, maziwa na chenji ya shilingi kumi

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Otieno atampa mama nini akirudi nyumbani?" with "pipi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za kifungu: mkate, maziwa na chenji ya shilingi kumi
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.

example.question: Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?
example.correct_answer: Tuwe waaminifu na tumrudishie mzazi chenji.

misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Otieno alienda dukani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tuwe waaminifu na tumrudishie mzazi chenji.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Otieno alipewa shilingi ngapi?" with "Mimi hupewa shilingi hamsini." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: shilingi mia moja
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa kisa (k.v. wahusika, ujumbe, muundo),
kusikiliza kisa kikitolewa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha,
kusoma kielelezo cha insha kwenye kitabu, chati au katika kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kutambua kanuni muhimu za uandishi (k.v. hati nadhifu, maudhui, mtiririko n.k.),
kuandika kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa na kujadili na wenzake; kisa hiki kifuate hatua tano za uandishi: maandalizi, nakala ya kwanza, urekebishaji, nakala safi na kuwasomea wenzake,
kumsomea kifungu kisha amwonyeshe mzazi au mlezi.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo gani tunazingatia katika uandishi wa insha?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki na kujadili na wenzake kutambua vipengele vya uandishi wa insha.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuandika insha.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli ya kuandika kifungu.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoandika kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa na kujadili na wenzake.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika ujifunzaji.
sub_strands.pcis:
Mahusiano ya kijamii: mwanafunzi anapowathamini wenzake na kushirikiana katika shughuli za uhariri.
Masuala ya kifedha: mwanafunzi anapoandika ufahamu kuhusu suala lengwa.

Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya uandishi wa insha anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa stadi hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua mambo ya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha
kuandika kisa cha kati ya maneno 85-90 kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia kanuni za uandishi
kufurahia uandishi wa visa tofauti ili kuimarisha mawasiliano andishi

skills.name: Andika kisa kifupi chenye mwanzo, kati na mwisho
skills.mastery: Writes a short story of about 85-90 words on dukani: a title that fits, sentences in order, one tense, Kiswahili words only, capitals and kikomo in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Ending sentences with the right mark comes before a whole story.
Writing a short paragraph about his surroundings (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Writes a list of sentences with no beginning, middle and end.
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks length makes a story.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kisa kizuri kina sehemu gani?" with "sentensi nyingi tu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Plan on three boxes: mwanzo (who, where), kati (what happened), mwisho (how it ended).
misconceptions.feedback: Kisa kina mwanzo, kati na mwisho.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes no title, or a title that does not fit the writing.

example.question: Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu dukani?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the word "insha" or the date is the title.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu dukani?" with "Insha" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the finished writing and ask: what is it about in three words?
misconceptions.feedback: Kichwa kinasema insha inahusu nini: Siku Nilipoenda Dukani.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins every sentence with "na halafu", so the writing is one long sentence.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Tuliamka asubuhi. Tulioga, kisha tukaenda sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: Spoken retelling joins events with na halafu; the child writes as he talks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a word bank: kwanza, kisha, baadaye, mwishowe; one per sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia kikomo na maneno kama kisha, baadaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Slips from one tense to another in the middle of the writing (past -li- to present -na-, or habitual hu- to past).
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of the events as he writes and the tense of the moment comes in.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Jana nilienda dukani. Ninanunua sukari." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline every verb; all the tense markers should match.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia wakati mmoja katika insha nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili writing.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the Kiswahili word and fills the gap with the one he knows.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha:" with "Nilinunua sugar na bread." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word bank of theme words on the board before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: Nilinunua sukari na mkate.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu (Theme 7: Dukani)
learning_experiences: kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, mti maneno, kapu maneno, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo kuhusu ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali na kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi hiyo,
kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi,
kutunga sentensi akitumia nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi na ukanushaji wake (kwa mfano: yeye anaandika - yeye haandiki),
kuigiza matumizi ya nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi na ukanushaji akiwa na wenzake,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi sentensi za nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi zilizokanushwa kuashiria vitendo vya watu mbalimbali nyumbani.
key_inquiry_questions: Unafikiri mwalimu wako alifanya nini jana? Iwapo hakufanya mambo uliyotaja ungesemaje?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi na ukanushaji wake.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: wanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kusikiliza wimbo au kifungu kuhusu ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapomsomea mzazi au mlezi kutumia ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja
sub_strands.values:
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kusikiliza wimbo au kifungu kuhusu ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nafsi ya tatu katika shughuli za kikundi.
Haki za jamii: mwanafunzi anapokanusha sentensi za nafsi ya tatu kuashiria vitendo vya watu mbalimbali nyumbani.

Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapowathamini wenzake wanaposhirikiana katika shughuli za ukanushaji.

outcomes.text: kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi
kutumia ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi kwa usahihi
kuchangamkia matumizi ya ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Kanusha sentensi za nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Makes the negative of a present-tense sentence in the third person: yeye anauza - yeye hauzi, wao wanauza - wao hawauzi (ha-/hawa-, no -na-, final -a to -i), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Yeye/wao and their subject markers come before their negatives.
The negative of the second person (Grade 2) shows the pattern.

misconceptions.error: Keeps the final -a in the negative present (hasoma for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child adds the negative prefix and leaves the rest of the verb as it was.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Yeye anauza sukari." with "Yeye hauza sukari." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the pair with the end of the verb circled: anasoma - hasomi.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika ukanushaji wa wakati uliopo, -a inakuwa -i: hasomi. (Yeye hauzi sukari.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the tense marker -na- in the negative (hanasomi for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child negates by adding ha- to the whole positive verb.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Yeye ananunua mkate." with "Yeye hananunui mkate." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cross out na in the positive form and change the end.
misconceptions.feedback: Hasomi: hakuna -na- katika ukanushaji huu. (Yeye hanunui mkate.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Negates by putting si before the positive verb (Yeye si anasoma).
misconceptions.cause: Si is the negative the child knows (si mimi), so he puts it in front of any sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Muuzaji anafungua duka." with "Muuzaji si anafungua duka." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show si as the negative of ni (Yeye si mwalimu) and ha- as the negative of a verb.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo hukanushwa kwa ha-: Yeye hasomi. (Muuzaji hafungui duka.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the negative prefix of another person (Wao hasomi for hawasomi; Mimi hasomi for sisomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child learnt one negative form (ha-) and uses it for all persons.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Wao wanauza maziwa." with "Wao hauzi maziwa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Table of persons: si-, hu-, ha-, hatu-, ham-, hawa-; the child points before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Wao hawasomi; mimi sisomi. (Wao hawauzi maziwa.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa (/mbw, /nd/, /ny/) katika kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, au kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kusikiliza maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua silabi lengwa,
kutamka maneno aliyosikiliza yenye sauti lengwa; atamke na mwalimu na mwishowe atamke akiwa na wenzake,
kusikiliza kwa makini sentensi zenye maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,

key_inquiry_questions: Je, matamshi bora hukuzwa kwa njia gani?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutambua na kutamka maneno yenye sauti lengwa.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali katika shughuli mbalimbali ili kuboresha matamshi yake.

sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake, kutambua na kutamka maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapothamini matamshi ya wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia na kutunza vifaa vya kidijitali katika shughuli inayorejelewa.

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /mbw/, /nd/, /ny/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /mbw/, /nd/, /ny/ in syllables and words (mbweha, ndege, nyumba), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Every syllable ends in a vowel; nd, ny and mbw start a syllable.
Saying words and sentences with target sounds (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Says /n/ for /ny/, so "nyama" becomes "nama".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "nyama". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /ny/, or do not separate it from /n/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "nyama". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "nama" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "nyama" ina sauti /ny/, si /n/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Pushes a vowel into the cluster, so "mbwa" is said "mubwa".
misconceptions.cause: In the child's first language, or in English loan habits, two consonants rarely sit together; he breaks them with a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tamka neno "mbwa". Ni lipi sahihi?" with "mubwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the cluster in one beat, then the word; clap once for the cluster syllable.
misconceptions.feedback: "mbwa" ina silabi mbwa; hakuna irabu ya ziada.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops part of the target sound, so "ndege" becomes "dege".

example.question: Neno "ndege" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The second part of the sound (the w or y glide, or the soft nasal) is quick and quiet; the child does not hear it and leaves it out.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "ndege" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?" with "dege" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stretch the syllable slowly (p-y-a), then say it fast; the child copies.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "ndege". Usiache sehemu ya sauti.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "mbweha" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "mbweha" lina silabi zipi?" with "m-b-w-e-h-a" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: mbwe-ha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /mbw/, /nd/, /ny/?" with "kuku" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "ndege" ina sauti lengwa; "kuku" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua sauti lengwa (/mbw, /nd/, /ny/) katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa sauti inayosikika akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 53 kwa dakika na kwa kuzingatia viakifishi),
kusoma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo akiwa na wenzake,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara zifaazo kwa ufasaha.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni kwa nini tunasoma kwa ufasaha?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kusoma kwa ufasaha.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kusoma hadithi kwa ufasaha.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposoma majarida na magazeti kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapojadiliana na wenzake na kusoma kifungu chepesi kwa ufasaha.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwa kikundi.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anapowashirikisha wengine katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali darasani.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali anavyovitumia.
sub_strands.pcis:
Elimu ya mazingira na tabia nchi: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara zifaazo.
Elimu ya utunzaji wa wanyama: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa.

kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo
kuchangamkia kusoma kwa ufasaha ili kufanikisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /mbw/, /nd/, /ny/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /mbw/, /nd/, /ny/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 53 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying mbw, nd and ny comes before reading them aloud.
Reading a short story with good pronunciation (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "nyumbani" as "numbani".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "nyumbani" linasomwa vipi?" with "numbani" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "nyumbani" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Ndege wangu anaimba asubuhi."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Ndege wangu anaimba asubuhi."?" with "Ndege ... wangu ... anaimba ... asubuhi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 53 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umemwona mbwa wa jirani?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umemwona mbwa wa jirani?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua tahajia sahihi za maneno katika uandishi wa insha kwenye kitabu au kifaa cha kidijitali,

kuandika insha akizingatia tahajia sahihi za maneno katika uandishi,
kurekebisha insha akizingatia tahajia za maneno,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi insha aliyoiandika kwa kuzingatia tahajia za maneno.
key_inquiry_questions: Kwa nini ni muhimu kuendeleza maneno ipasavyo unapoandika chochote?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za ujifunzaji.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kujifunza tahajia sahihi za maneno katika insha.

Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika insha kwa kuzingatia tahajia za maneno.

Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapoandika insha akizingatia tahajia sahihi.
