outcomes.text: kutambua tahajia sahihi za maneno katika insha
kuandika insha akizingatia tahajia sahihi za maneno
kufurahia kutumia tahajia sahihi katika maandishi

skills.name: Andika insha fupi kwa tahajia sahihi za maneno
skills.mastery: Writes the words of his own writing (about 85-90 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Spelling words from dictation comes before spelling in his own insha.
Writing sentences with correct spelling (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "rangi" written "langi".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "langi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "rangi" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "mbawa" written "bawa".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "bawa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "mbawa" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "paa" written "pa".

example.question: Andika neno lenye maana ya "sehemu ya juu ya nyumba".

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "sehemu ya juu ya nyumba"." with "pa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "paa" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya Maneno Hili na Haya (Theme 8: Ndege nimpendaye)
learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya neno hili na haya (k.v. jicho hili – macho haya, jino hili – meno haya n.k.) katika kifungu kwenye chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake,
kusoma sentensi zinazoonyesha matumizi ya neno hili na haya katika kifungu akishirikiana na wenzake,

key_inquiry_questions: Ni maneno yapi yanayoambatanishwa na maneno hili na haya?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuchangia kikamilifu katika shughuli za kikundi.

Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia matumizi ya neno hili na haya.
Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotumia neno hili na haya kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake.

Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutunga sentensi akitumia neno hili na haya ipasavyo
Amani: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali na wenzake ili kutambua na kutunga sentensi akitumia hili na haya kwa utulivu.

outcomes.text: kutambua matumizi ya neno hili na haya katika kifungu
kutumia neno hili na haya katika kifungu ili kuboresha mawasiliano
kuchangamkia matumizi ya hili na haya katika mawasiliano

skills.name: Tumia hili na haya ipasavyo katika kifungu
skills.mastery: Uses hili with a near li-ma noun in the singular and haya in the plural (yai hili - mayai haya, jicho hili - macho haya), not huyu or hii, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Yule and wale (Theme 3) are the first pointing words that change with number.
The li-ma plurals (jino - meno) come from Theme 4.
Huyo and hao (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Uses the people word (huyu, yule) for a thing (kiti huyu).
misconceptions.cause: Huyu was the first pointing word learnt; the child uses it for anything.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Yai ___ ni bovu." with "huyu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Point at a child (huyu) and at a chair (hiki); then sort pictures by the pointing word they take.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitu cha ngeli ya ki-vi huonyeshwa kwa hiki; mtu huonyeshwa kwa huyu. (hili)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the one-thing pointing word with a plural noun (watoto huyu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun but not the pointing word.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Mayai ___ ni mabovu." with "hili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair the forms on cards: huyu-hawa, yule-wale, hiki-hivi, hili-haya.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto ni wengi: watoto hawa. (haya)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
misconceptions.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "jicho hili" ni?" with "majicho haya" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
misconceptions.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (macho haya)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses hii for every noun (kitabu hii, mtoto hii), as in town Kiswahili.
misconceptions.cause: Hii is the pointing word heard most in town speech, where the noun class is dropped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Jani ___ ni la kijani." with "hii" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: kitabu hiki, mtoto huyu, nyumba hii; the child hears the match.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu hiki; mtoto huyu; nyumba hii. (hili)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua suala lengwa linalozungumziwa kupitia kwa picha kutoka kwenye kitabu, chati, vifaa vya kidijitali pamoja na wenzake,
kuchukua muda wa kufikiri kuhusu suala la kuzungumzia,
kupanga mawazo yake kuhusu suala lengwa na kuandaa hoja za kuzungumzia,
kutamka maneno kwa kuzingatia matamshi yafaayo ya sauti mbalimbali,

kupandisha na kushusha sauti panapohitajika,
kutumia ishara mbalimbali zinazohusiana na maelezo yake kuhusu suala lengwa,

key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia nini unapozungumza kuhusu masuala mbalimbali?

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki mazungumzo na wenzake katika kikundi.

Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki mazungumzo ya kila siku ili kuimarisha mawasiliano.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapojieleza kwa ufasaha mbele ya wenzake.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwenye kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali na nyenzo nyinginezo anazotumia kujifunzia.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowasikiliza wenzake darasani na kuheshimu maoni yao.
sub_strands.pcis: Elimu ya kifedha: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza mazungumzo kuhusu suala lengwa.

skills.name: Shiriki mazungumzo kuhusu bidhaa za sokoni kwa zamu, kwa matamshi bora na ishara zifaazo
skills.mastery: Takes part in a short conversation about bidhaa za sokoni: keeps to the topic, waits for his turn, speaks Kiswahili without English or Sheng words, says sounds clearly and uses gestures that match the words, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Speaking fluently in an unprepared talk (Grade 2) comes first.
Listening for what others say is half of a conversation.

misconceptions.error: Says something that has nothing to do with the topic.

example.question: Mnazungumza kuhusu bidhaa za sokoni. Ni sentensi ipi inafaa?

misconceptions.cause: The child says what is on his mind; he has not learnt that a conversation has a topic everyone keeps to.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mnazungumza kuhusu bidhaa za sokoni. Ni sentensi ipi inafaa?" with "Jana nilitazama katuni nzuri." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put the topic picture in the middle; before speaking the child points to it.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunazungumza kuhusu bidhaa za sokoni; sema jambo kuhusu hilo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Talks over others and does not wait for his turn.
misconceptions.cause: Eagerness: the child fears he will forget his idea.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwenzako anazungumza. Unafanya nini?" with "ninaanza kuzungumza pia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pass a talking object (a ball): only the one holding it speaks.
misconceptions.feedback: Subiri zamu yako; msikilize mwenzako kwanza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili sentence.
misconceptions.cause: At home and in town the child hears mixed speech and does not know the Kiswahili word.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sema kwa Kiswahili sanifu:" with "Tulienda market tukabuy tomatoes." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word wall: the English or Sheng word, and its Kiswahili word next to it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunasema: Tulienda sokoni tukanunua nyanya.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a gesture or face that does not match the words (smiling while giving sad news).

example.question: Unasema "Rafiki yangu ni mgonjwa." Uso wako unaonyesha nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child smiles from shyness or does not link the face to the message.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unasema "Rafiki yangu ni mgonjwa." Uso wako unaonyesha nini?" with "tabasamu kubwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say one sentence with three faces; the class picks the face that fits.
misconceptions.feedback: Ishara zako zifuate ujumbe wako.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /l/ for /r/ (or /r/ for /l/) while speaking: "rafiki" becomes "lafiki".
misconceptions.cause: Several Kenyan first languages do not separate /l/ and /r/; the home sound carries into Kiswahili.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tamka vizuri: rafiki" with "lafiki" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Practise the pairs with a mirror: the tongue taps for r, it rests for l.
misconceptions.feedback: Tamka "rafiki" kwa /r/: ulimi unagonga mara moja.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 70- 75 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa akiwa na wenzake,
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,
kutabiri kitakachotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu kwa kuzingatia picha akiwa na wenzake,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha hadithi akiwa na wenzake,
kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha hadithi akiwa na wenzake,
kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu hadithi kama akiwa na wenzake,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa na kujadili ujumbe.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo yapi unayozingatia unaposoma kifungu chochote?

Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposoma majarida na magazeti kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma.

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on sokoni, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The comprehension questions of Theme 7 come first.
Predicting what will happen in a short passage (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Gives "wateja" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Bi. Neema huuza matunda sokoni. Ana maembe, machungwa na mananasi. Wateja wengi hununua matunda yake kwa sababu ni safi na matamu." Neno "wateja" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Bi. Neema huuza matunda sokoni. Ana maembe, machungwa na mananasi. Wateja wengi hununua matunda yake kwa sababu ni safi na matamu." Neno "wateja" lina maana gani?" with "watoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "wateja" ni watu wanaonunua bidhaa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tukiuza bidhaa safi tunapata wateja wengi.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Bi. Neema ana maembe." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tukiuza bidhaa safi tunapata wateja wengi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha mawingu meusi juu ya soko. Nini kitatokea?
example.correct_answer: Mvua itanyesha na wauzaji watafunika bidhaa zao.

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha mawingu meusi juu ya soko. Nini kitatokea?" with "Jua kali litawaka." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Mvua itanyesha na wauzaji watafunika bidhaa zao.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.

example.question: Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?
example.correct_answer: Tunapaswa kuwa safi na waaminifu katika kazi zetu.

misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Bi. Neema huuza matunda." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kuwa safi na waaminifu katika kazi zetu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Bi. Neema huuza nini?" with "Mama yangu huuza sukumawiki." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: matunda
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusikiliza masimulizi yakitolewa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali,
kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha ya masimulizi kutoka kwenye masimulizi aliyosikiliza,
kusoma kielelezo cha insha ya masimulizi kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali kuhusu insha ya masimulizi akiwa na wenzake,
kutambua mambo muhimu katika uandishi wa insha katika kielelezo cha insha aliyosoma,
kuandika kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa; kisa hiki kifuate hatua za uandishi: maandalizi, nakala ya kwanza, urekebishaji, nakala safi na kuwasomea wenzake,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa ili akitolee maoni.

Je,kisa ulichowahi kusimuliwa kilikuwa na mafunzo gani?

Uwazaji wa kina: mwanafunzi anapotambua mambo yanayotakikana katika uandishi wa insha ya masimulizi.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika insha ya masimulizi kwa kuzingatia vipengele husika.

skills.name: Andika insha fupi ya masimulizi
skills.mastery: Writes a short insha ya masimulizi of about 85-90 words on sokoni: a title that fits, sentences in order, one tense, Kiswahili words only, capitals and kikomo in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: A story with a beginning, middle and end (Theme 7) comes first.
Retelling events in order is the spoken form of a narrative.

misconceptions.error: Writes a list of sentences with no beginning, middle and end.
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks length makes a story.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kisa kizuri kina sehemu gani?" with "sentensi nyingi tu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Plan on three boxes: mwanzo (who, where), kati (what happened), mwisho (how it ended).
misconceptions.feedback: Kisa kina mwanzo, kati na mwisho.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes no title, or a title that does not fit the writing.

example.question: Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu sokoni?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the word "insha" or the date is the title.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu sokoni?" with "Insha" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the finished writing and ask: what is it about in three words?
misconceptions.feedback: Kichwa kinasema insha inahusu nini: Safari Yangu ya Sokoni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins every sentence with "na halafu", so the writing is one long sentence.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Tuliamka asubuhi. Tulioga, kisha tukaenda sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: Spoken retelling joins events with na halafu; the child writes as he talks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a word bank: kwanza, kisha, baadaye, mwishowe; one per sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia kikomo na maneno kama kisha, baadaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Slips from one tense to another in the middle of the writing (past -li- to present -na-, or habitual hu- to past).

example.question: Ni lipi sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Tulifika sokoni mapema. Mama ananunua ndizi.
example.correct_answer: Tulifika sokoni mapema. Mama alinunua ndizi.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of the events as he writes and the tense of the moment comes in.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Tulifika sokoni mapema. Mama ananunua ndizi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline every verb; all the tense markers should match.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia wakati mmoja katika insha nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili writing.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the Kiswahili word and fills the gap with the one he knows.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha:" with "Tulinunua sukuma na onions." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word bank of theme words on the board before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: Tulinunua sukumawiki na vitunguu.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika matini,
kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo unaotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya kutoka kwa mgeni mwalikwa, mwalimu au vifaa vya kidijitali na kutambua matumizi yazo akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu kilichotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake,
kujadili na mwenzake matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika kifungu ili kutolea maoni,
kujaza nafasi ili kukamilisha sentensi zilizotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake,
kutunga sentensi akitumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake,

kuigiza matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake kwa kutumia vitu anavyomiliki (k.m; Mboga iko ndani ya gunia, Vitabu viko juu ya rafu, Kitabu kiko ndani ya mkoba, Gari liko mbele ya duka),
kumtungia mzazi au mlezi wake sentensi kwa kutumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya kwa kuzingatia vitu katika mazingira ya nyumbani.

kutumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika sentensi
kuchangamkia matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Tumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Says where something is with juu ya, ndani ya and mbele ya (and their opposites chini ya, nje ya, nyuma ya), keeping ya and not adding -ni to the noun, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Direction words in instructions (juu, chini, kulia) come first.
Writing two-word groups (Grade 2) comes before three-word place phrases.

misconceptions.error: Leaves out ya (juu meza for juu ya meza).
misconceptions.cause: In fast speech ya is quick and the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Ndizi ziko juu meza." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the phrase slowly with a clap on ya.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunasema "juu ya meza". (Ndizi ziko juu ya meza.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses kwa in place of ya (ndani kwa sanduku).
misconceptions.cause: Kwa is a common joining word and the child reaches for it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Machungwa yako ndani kwa kikapu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair cards: juu ya, ndani ya, mbele ya; kwa is not among them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunasema "ndani ya sanduku". (Machungwa yako ndani ya kikapu.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes the place words (juu ya for chini ya, mbele ya for nyuma ya).

example.question: Muuzaji amesimama mbele ya kibanda. Yuko wapi?

misconceptions.cause: The pairs are learnt together and swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Muuzaji amesimama mbele ya kibanda. Yuko wapi?" with "nyuma ya kibanda" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Place a real ball on, under, in, in front of a box; the child says where.
misconceptions.feedback: Angalia tena mpira ulipo. (mbele ya kibanda)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Adds -ni to the noun as well as ndani ya (ndani ya sandukuni).
misconceptions.cause: Both ways of saying "in" are known; the child uses both at once.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Pesa ziko ndani ya mfukoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the two ways side by side: sandukuni, or ndani ya sanduku; never both.
misconceptions.feedback: Sema "ndani ya sanduku" au "sandukuni", si vyote viwili. (Pesa ziko ndani ya mfuko.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /mb/, /nz/, /tw/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /mb/, /nz/, /tw/ in syllables and words (mbali, nzuri, twiga), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The nasal clusters nd and mbw come before mb and nz.
Hearing target syllables in words (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Says /ns/ for /nz/, so "nzuri" becomes "nsuri".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "nzuri". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /nz/, or do not separate it from /ns/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "nzuri". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "nsuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "nzuri" ina sauti /nz/, si /ns/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Pushes a vowel into the cluster, so "twiga" is said "tuwiga".
misconceptions.cause: In the child's first language, or in English loan habits, two consonants rarely sit together; he breaks them with a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tamka neno "twiga". Ni lipi sahihi?" with "tuwiga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the cluster in one beat, then the word; clap once for the cluster syllable.
misconceptions.feedback: "twiga" ina silabi twi-ga; hakuna irabu ya ziada.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops part of the target sound, so "mbali" becomes "bali".

example.question: Neno "mbali" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The second part of the sound (the w or y glide, or the soft nasal) is quick and quiet; the child does not hear it and leaves it out.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "mbali" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?" with "bali" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stretch the syllable slowly (p-y-a), then say it fast; the child copies.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "mbali". Usiache sehemu ya sauti.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "mbali" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "mbali" lina silabi zipi?" with "m-b-a-l-i" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: mba-li.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /mb/, /nz/, /tw/?" with "redio" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "nzuri" ina sauti lengwa; "redio" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /mb/, /nz/, /tw/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /mb/, /nz/, /tw/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 55 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying mb, nz and tw comes before reading them aloud.
Reading at a fitting pace (Grade 2).

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "twende" as "tuwende".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "twende" linasomwa vipi?" with "tuwende" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "twende" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana simu mpya ya kisasa."?
example.wrong_answer: Mama ... ana ... simu ... mpya ... ya ... kisasa.
example.correct_answer: Mama ana simu mpya ya kisasa.

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana simu mpya ya kisasa."?" with "Mama ... ana ... simu ... mpya ... ya ... kisasa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 55 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, simu hii ni nzuri?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, simu hii ni nzuri?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika insha fupi ya maelezo
skills.mastery: Writes a short insha ya maelezo of about 85-90 words on teknolojia: a title that fits, sentences in order, one tense, Kiswahili words only, capitals and kikomo in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Planning and writing a short insha (Theme 7) comes first.
Editing his own writing (Grade 2) before the clean copy.

misconceptions.error: Tells a story of events instead of describing the thing (what it is, what it looks like, what it is for).

example.question: Insha ya maelezo kuhusu "Simu" inaanza vipi?

misconceptions.cause: Every insha the child has written before was a story.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Insha ya maelezo kuhusu "Simu" inaanza vipi?" with "Siku moja nilienda mjini..." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give three question cards: Ni nini? Kinaonekanaje? Kinatumiwaje? One aya each.
misconceptions.feedback: Insha ya maelezo inaeleza kitu kilivyo na kazi yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes no title, or a title that does not fit the writing.

example.question: Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu teknolojia?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the word "insha" or the date is the title.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu teknolojia?" with "Insha" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the finished writing and ask: what is it about in three words?
misconceptions.feedback: Kichwa kinasema insha inahusu nini: Simu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins every sentence with "na halafu", so the writing is one long sentence.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Tuliamka asubuhi. Tulioga, kisha tukaenda sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: Spoken retelling joins events with na halafu; the child writes as he talks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a word bank: kwanza, kisha, baadaye, mwishowe; one per sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia kikomo na maneno kama kisha, baadaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Slips from one tense to another in the middle of the writing (past -li- to present -na-, or habitual hu- to past).

example.question: Ni lipi sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Simu hutumika kuwasiliana. Iliwasaidia watu kuzungumza.
example.correct_answer: Simu hutumika kuwasiliana. Huwasaidia watu kuzungumza.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of the events as he writes and the tense of the moment comes in.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Simu hutumika kuwasiliana. Iliwasaidia watu kuzungumza." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline every verb; all the tense markers should match.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia wakati mmoja katika insha nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili writing.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the Kiswahili word and fills the gap with the one he knows.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha:" with "Simu ina screen na battery." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word bank of theme words on the board before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: Simu ina skrini na betri.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utumie vinyume vya vitendo
skills.mastery: Gives and uses the opposite action of a verb (fungua - funga, washa - zima, keti - simama, ingia - toka), not its negative, a word of the same meaning, or a place word, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Opposite actions in sentences (Grade 2) come first.
Knowing the negative lets the child tell it from the opposite.

misconceptions.error: Gives the negative of the verb (hafungui) instead of its opposite action (funga).
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks "opposite" means "not doing it".
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "washa" (redio) ni?" with "usiwashe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act it: fungua the door, then funga it; not doing anything is not the opposite.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha kitendo ni kitendo kingine: fungua - funga. (zima)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes an opposite by adding -ua to any verb (keti -> ketua).
misconceptions.cause: Fungua/funga and vaa/vua show a pattern, and the child uses it everywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "keti" ni?" with "ketua" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort pairs into two piles: made with -ua (funga-fungua) and different words (keti-simama).
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha keti ni simama. (simama)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a word of the same meaning as the opposite (simama - inuka).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the words go together but not that they mean the same.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "simama" ni?" with "inuka" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act both words: if the action is the same, it is not the opposite.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume ni kitendo kinachopingana. (keti)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a place or thing word as the opposite of an action (ingia - nje).
misconceptions.cause: Ingia and nje are heard together in "ingia ndani, toka nje".
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "ingia" ni?" with "nje" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask "Ni kitendo?" before accepting: the opposite of an action is an action.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha ingia ni toka. (toka)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher
